profile.beat: Sector-rotation and relative-strength (RS) technician who covers US equity sectors, credit spreads, rates, gold, energy and macro, and speaks to clients and appears on interviews and shows.
profile.style: Chart-first, and he describes himself as sector-oriented rather than driven by index levels. Most calls are one-line captions on RS or chart images (bear flags, bases) with heavy sarcasm; he rarely sizes positions but occasionally discloses one (FAZ, short for weeks). He often reminds readers of earlier calls he got right.
profile.cadence: High-volume: roughly 146 posts over the week, mostly short replies and quote-tweets, plus bursts of ticker-caption chart posts (a bank/insurance burst on 2026-09-22, a consumer/credit burst on 2026-09-24). Recurring posts on high-yield spreads, the MOVE index and 10-year yields.
profile.revisits: Yes. He returns to banks several times (2102406034954273112, 2102975512884973676, 2103135764989030780), revisits SCL on the inflation pass-through theme (2102791180702683635), revisits the MOVE level-85 call (2102217601032093798, 2103220139306914105), and repeats his earlier gold and Bitcoin calls (2102567103085588901, 2102597575882813804).
profile.caveats: Most posts are captions on chart images that are not in the corpus, so the evidence behind many calls cannot be seen. Several bearish calls (insurers, banks, auto dealers, travel) are posted after the move is already underway. The account often claims past calls were right, and those claims cannot be verified here. Heavy sarcasm makes some posts hard to read as a direction.

narrative: Over the week the author argues that breadth is badly deteriorating under a market held up by crowded tech, energy and healthcare. He says late-cycle money is crowding into the most liquid names and that 'generals last' signals a bigger decline. On 2026-09-22 he turns this into a bank call: he flags JPM for multiple compression, a GS bear flag and an MS top, and discloses a FAZ position and a short he has held for weeks. On 2026-09-23 hot flash PMIs push him to mock the disinflation camp. He leans into inflation beneficiaries with pricing power (chemicals SCL and CE), bullish flags in gold and silver miners, and bearish REITs on CRE markdowns and likely dividend cuts. On 2026-09-24 he widens the bearish view to consumer discretionary: travel, casinos, cruise lines, auto dealers, auto lending and FDX. He calls market-wide multiple compression and predicts a regional bank crisis, driven by corporate debt issuance competing with Treasuries and widening high-yield spreads. He ends the week tempering slightly. He says rising bond rates only slow the rise in equities, and he wants to see oversold sectors bounce.
